idiom_name: template<typename T> Channel over std::queue + std::mutex/std::condition_variable
implementation_notes: The standard library has no channel type, so the datatype channel is hand-written: one Channel<T> instance per message type, with the template parameter as the channel's identity, std::queue<T> as the buffer and a std::mutex/std::condition_variable pair for the transfer; send()/receive() replace the runtime question 'what type is this?' because the compiler will not let an Invoice be pushed into the order channel. The handwritten structure is still justified exactly when you need control over blocking, capacity, cancellation and shutdown; write it once as a template and instantiate it per type rather than hand-rolling a queue per message type. In middleware code the same rule shows up as one AMQP routing key, Kafka topic or ZeroMQ topic per message type with a per-type codec - do not multiplex several types onto one topic and demultiplex with dynamic_cast or a tag field.
pitfalls: std::condition_variable::wait must be called through the predicated overload or re-checked in a loop: spurious wakeups otherwise hand the consumer an empty queue.
One Channel<T> shared by reference across threads has no implicit shutdown: blocked receivers are not woken by destruction, so notify_all plus a closed flag belongs in the type.
Every payload is copied (or moved) through the queue: for large T store a shared_ptr/unique_ptr or the channel becomes the pipeline's bottleneck.
